projects.name: Refugee resettlement
projects.description: In close coordination with UNHCR, the Malaysian Government and the governments of receiving countries, IOM facilitates safe and orderly resettlement of vulnerable refugees and asylum seekers to third countries. As a result of these initiatives, the most vulnerable individuals including those with significant medical conditions from over 20 nationalities were able to start new lives in more than 10 host countries, where they have access to healthcare, employment, formal education, and pathways to citizenship. In CY 2022 IOM facilitated the resettlement of 4,367 refugees including medical screening, vaccinations and treatment for communicable diseases, and cultural orientation prior to departure to a new country. Resettlement and complimentary pathways are a vital protection tool to provide international protection and meet the specific needs of refugees in which life, liberty, safety, health or fundamental human rights are secured.
projects.outcome: A more efficient, effective and sustainable social protection system is in place that provides increased protection against contingencies throughout the lifecycle.

projects.name: UN Joint Team on HIV and AIDS in Malaysia
projects.description:
The Joint Team rendered substantial support to the Malaysian Government in ensuring sustainable funding, advancing prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV services and expanding HIV services to hard-to-reach communities. Technical support to the Malaysian Country Coordinating Mechanism and the Malaysian AIDS Council led to a successful Global Fund for HIV grant proposal for the 2022-2025 period. Focused on the establishment of resilient and sustainable systems for health (RSSH) and the expansion of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) as a method of HIV prevention, the application secured US$ 1.5 million for the procurement of PrEP for 18 primary care clinics across Malaysia until December 2024. More than US$ 1 million was also allocated to strengthen community-led programmes, the national health management information system, and monitoring and evaluation for RSSH (WHO).

Malaysia achieved all the process and outcome indicator targets set in the Elimination of Mother-to-child Transmission of HIV (EMTCT) and Syphilis plan for the 2017-2020 period. In 2022, the Joint Team provided extensive technical support for the development and submission of the EMTCT maintenance report and worked closely with the Regional and Global Validation Secretariat and the Ministry of Health to address concerns including human rights, gender equality and community engagement, which were raised by Global Validation Advisory Committee (GVAC) during its 2021 virtual mission (WHO).

The newly launched Reaching the Unreached (RTU) agenda helped to identify key cross-cutting issues affecting marginalized populations, including the high prevalence of communicable diseases such as tuberculosis in East Malaysia and in prisons and other closed settings through a collaboration with relevant stakeholders (WHO). Intense advocacy and technical support to the Ministry of Health also resulted in the Government recognizing the need to strengthen laboratory capacity by expanding point-of-care testing systems in high-burden areas to eliminate logistical barriers and improve access to healthcare services (WHO).

To expand access to HIV services among key and vulnerable populations, 138 refugees and asylum seekers living with HIV accessed antiretroviral treatment with support from the Joint Team. Nongovernmental organizations also received support in providing treatment adherence support services for 172 persons living with HIV enrolled on treatment, rehabilitative and nursing care for 12 extremely vulnerable refugees as well as sexual and reproductive health, gender-based violence and HIV information and counselling services for 935 hard-to-reach women and girls and their spouses through regular mobile outreach programmes in the Northern region of the Peninsular Malaysia. Additionally, 128 pregnant women and girls received antenatal care while 270 were given regular access to contraceptives through the mobile programmes (UNHCR).

Technical assistance was provided to the National Anti-drugs Agency of Malaysia on the transition towards voluntary-community based treatment and care of people who use drugs, as well as on “Strong Families” family-skills substance use prevention among children and adolescents. The Malaysian Prisons Department also benefitted from technical support on the delivery of comprehensive packages of HIV services for people in prisons (UNODC).

projects.name: Addressing marine litter in South-East Asia
projects.description:
Under this project, Mersing Islands (Malaysia) to demonstrate integrated waste management good practices in remote/island communities to reduce and prevent plastic waste leakage into the coastal and marine environment in line with the Regional Action Plan on Marine Litter (RAP MALI). 

Prior to project activities, no waste management practices existed in the Mersing Islands and plastic waste was largely littered or burned. Through the pilot, an integral waste management system was created with the community, and the population received education on reducing and segregating plastic for recycling and disposal. This includes the use of a plastic compacting machine and simple disposal and sorting infrastructure, so recyclables can be processed and taken to the mainland to be recycled. 

The pilot was implemented in partnership with Reef-Check Malaysia (USD 55,000 SSFA).

projects.name: Unwaste: tackling waste trafficking to support a circular economy in South East Asia.
projects.description:
Implemented by UNODC in cooperation with UNEP and UNITAR, aims to fight trafficking in waste between the EU and Southeast Asia. It does so by promoting enhanced EU-ASEAN Member States partnerships, in support of ongoing efforts towards a circular economy transition, in line with the relevant policy frameworks, with four priority countries: Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam. 
UNEP is responsible for the legal components, examining the legal framework in the ASEAN region on waste trafficking and a legal comparative analysis of the four priority countries. UNEP will also develop a policy paper on ‘obstacles waste trafficking poses to the develop of circular economy and best practices from EU and Asia’, and a mapping of existing multilateral mechanisms in place in Southeast Asia to prevent waste trafficking in support of the objectives of the Unwaste project.

projects.name: Understanding Pathways to Adolescent Pregnancy in Southeast Asia
projects.description:
This study, conducted in Malaysia as part of a wider Southeast Asia study, is a collaboration between the Burnet Institute, UNFPA, and UNICEF. The study aims to improve understanding of the drivers and pathways to adolescent pregnancy in Southeast Asia and inform effective policy and programming responses. The primary objective of the study is to identify and explore the drivers and pathways to both intended and unintended adolescent pregnancy in Southeast Asia, including the relationship with early marriage/union. The study's secondary objective is to develop policy and programming recommendations, co-created with adolescents, to effectively address adolescent pregnancy.

The report was launched on 18 October 2023 as a joint initiative by UNFPA Malaysia and UNICEF Malaysia and was developed by the Burnet Institute.  The report included in-depth interviews with 45 adolescent girls from three states in Malaysia – Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, and Pahang, and highlighted six pathways to adolescent pregnancy. The reports underscore the importance of adolescent-responsive health services, comprehensive sexuality education, supportive relationships, and enabling environments that empower girls to make informed decisions about their sexual and reproductive health and lives.
projects.outcome: Increased adoption of inclusive social norms and values and rejection of harmful practices, particularly against women and girls, and the creation of demand for services

projects.name: Mobilising Stakeholders to Inform the Development of a Science-based decision Support System for Coastal Wetlands in the ASEAN Region
projects.description: This project aimed to generate informed recommendations and ideas for the development of an online knowledge sharing platform in the ASEAN region to support science-based decision system for coastal and marine biodiversity conservation and management. The project involved a stakeholder consultation process to explore the information and marine conservation capacity needs of natural resource managers, the business sector, and government organizations. This process of national and regional consultation was held with representatives and stakeholders from all 10 ASEAN Member States, and included national workshops, a regional experts forum, and an online survey. These activities were structured with the view to inform the design of the new platform. UNEP-WCMC provided technical advice and input on the consultations, and produced a discussion paper that synthesised all results and provided recommendations on development of the online knowledge sharing platform. This discussion paper is now being finalised, and a Phase 2 of the project is hoping to be developed to pursue development of the platform.
projects.outcome: Natural resources, biodiversity and ecosystems are sustainably managed, adequately protected and conserved for long-term economic and environmental sustainability.

projects.name: UN Joint Team on HIV and AIDS in Malaysia
projects.description:
The Joint Team rendered substantial support to the Malaysian Government in ensuring sustainable funding, advancing prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV services and expanding HIV services to hard-to-reach communities. Technical support to the Malaysian Country Coordinating Mechanism and the Malaysian AIDS Council led to a successful Global Fund for HIV grant proposal for the 2022-2025 period. Focused on the establishment of resilient and sustainable systems for health (RSSH) and the expansion of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) as a method of HIV prevention, the application secured US$ 1.5 million for the procurement of PrEP for 18 primary care clinics across Malaysia until December 2024. More than US$ 1 million was also allocated to strengthen community-led programmes, the national health management information system, and monitoring and evaluation for RSSH (WHO).

Malaysia achieved all the process and outcome indicator targets set in the Elimination of Mother-to-child Transmission of HIV (EMTCT) and Syphilis plan for the 2017-2020 period. In 2022, the Joint Team provided extensive technical support for the development and submission of the EMTCT maintenance report and worked closely with the Regional and Global Validation Secretariat and the Ministry of Health to address concerns including human rights, gender equality and community engagement, which were raised by Global Validation Advisory Committee (GVAC) during its 2021 virtual mission (WHO).

The newly launched Reaching the Unreached (RTU) agenda helped to identify key cross-cutting issues affecting marginalized populations, including the high prevalence of communicable diseases such as tuberculosis in East Malaysia and in prisons and other closed settings through a collaboration with relevant stakeholders (WHO). Intense advocacy and technical support to the Ministry of Health also resulted in the Government recognizing the need to strengthen laboratory capacity by expanding point-of-care testing systems in high-burden areas to eliminate logistical barriers and improve access to healthcare services (WHO).

To expand access to HIV services among key and vulnerable populations, 138 refugees and asylum seekers living with HIV accessed antiretroviral treatment with support from the Joint Team. Nongovernmental organizations also received support in providing treatment adherence support services for 172 persons living with HIV enrolled on treatment, rehabilitative and nursing care for 12 extremely vulnerable refugees as well as sexual and reproductive health, gender-based violence and HIV information and counselling services for 935 hard-to-reach women and girls and their spouses through regular mobile outreach programmes in the Northern region of the Peninsular Malaysia. Additionally, 128 pregnant women and girls received antenatal care while 270 were given regular access to contraceptives through the mobile programmes (UNHCR).

Technical assistance was provided to the National Anti-drugs Agency of Malaysia on the transition towards voluntary-community based treatment and care of people who use drugs, as well as on “Strong Families” family-skills substance use prevention among children and adolescents. The Malaysian Prisons Department also benefitted from technical support on the delivery of comprehensive packages of HIV services for people in prisons (UNODC).
projects.outcome: Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.

projects.name: Ecosystems (policy, standards, and technologies) enabled to allow Malaysia to harness solar thermal energy as one of renewable energy sources contributing to the country's GHG emission targets
projects.description:
efficiency and application of solar thermal systems in Malaysia” started its implementation in July 2014 and completed in June 2022. 
The project was promoted and branded as the “Malaysia Energy Efficiency and Solar Thermal Application Project” (MAEESTA). The Malaysia Energy Efficiency and Solar Thermal Application Project (MAEESTA) which started being implemented in July 2014 was initially designed for a five-year duration. However, due to challenges faced while implementing the project especially to convince companies to invest in implementing energy efficiency measures and in the demonstration plant, and due to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic which started affecting the country in early 2020, the project was approved to be extended for another three years, i.e. until June 2022.
The project’s objective was to reduce greenhouse gases (GHG) emissions by promoting and demonstrating sector-specific energy efficiency (EE) improvements and solar thermal technology utilization in industry. The industrial sub-sectors stated in the project’s document mainly cover the raw material processing and manufacturing sectors. The hospitality sector (hotels and hospitals) was agreed to be included as one of the focused industrial sub-sectors during the second National Project Steering Committee (NPSC) meeting held on 16th December 2016. 

The project completed in June 2022. More details on achievements will be provided shortly.

projects.name: Dementia Care Skills Training Workshop for Caregivers
projects.description:
Dementia Care Skills Training Workshop for Caregivers as a program being adopted from Alzheimer’s Disease International where guidelines to develop the local content needs, Training Modules are modified to suit the local requirements.

The objectives of the training workshop are:
•Provide an understanding of Dementia
•Learning about the Impact of Dementia and how Person-Centred Care is important
•Communication Effectively with a Person with Dementia
•Importance on how to address Behavioural & Psychological Symptoms of Dementia
•Understanding Meaningful Activities and Engagement and how best to manage and roll out these activities
•Knowledge of Legal /Ethical Issues and the importance of Advanced Care Planning
• Pre-tests were conducted at the start of the Training session to determine the level of understanding of Dementia, Stages, and care skill
•Post-Test is also being conducted at the end of the course to understand how the Training Workshop had helped them in the understanding and Care for Person with Dementia
•VARK methodology was used in the Training Workshop as studies have proven Visual, Audiology, Reading/Writing, and Kinesthetic approach have a better way to retain what had been taught through the way of repeating the scenario in action.

The target audience for this Training Workshop were volunteers from Ministry of Health / Ministry of Welfare programs and the majority of volunteers had informal caregiving experience but not Dementia Care Skills.

projects.name: Survey of salt levels in street foods to strengthen salt reduction action in Malaysia
projects.description:
This project will strengthen the implementation of  Malaysia’s  Salt  Reduction Strategy through generating data about the salt levels in street foods and meals in Malaysia, with a view to: 
(1) providing evidence for accelerating the introduction of mandatory sodium labelling on packaged and street foods, 
(2) informing salt-reduction education messages about what high-salt foods to avoid and what alternatives to consume as part of a strategic behavior change communication plan; and
(3) identifying and engaging food industries producing high-salt foods in reformulation. Analysis of the sodium content will be conducted on street foods which include ready-to-eat foods usually sold by small- to medium-sized vendors in a street, hawker center, or food court. 
This proposal extends ongoing national salt reduction efforts since 2015 and a recent mid-term evaluation of its progress, which elucidated areas for enhancement to ensure the targeted 15% reduction in population salt intake is achieved by 2020.

projects.name: Social listening and rumours and misinformation management
projects.description:
Data collection conducted in partnership with research company, Media Measurement (MM) from the UK, to inform decision and policy making, including strategic communications at MOH. Activities included following online conversational trends related to COVID-19 and COVID-19 vaccines, both in terms of volume and velocity, and a weekly in-depth analysis of not just prominent topics but the emotional and behavioural responses that result. 

Work also includes provision of daily reports as snapshots of the most important online conversations and rumours and misinformation so that MOH can quickly pick up on and respond to these issues. In addition, a rumours and misinformation alert system and repository were created to track their impact and facilitate timely response. Additionally, there is bi-yearly, in-depth analysis of all key topics related to COVID-19, based on the methodology proposed by MM.

projects.name: Capacity building for economic evaluation and modelling for infectious disease outbreaks with a focus on the case of the COVID-19 pandemic
projects.description:
WCO collaborated with the School of Population and Global Health, University of Melbourne, to build the capacity for economic evaluation and modelling for infectious disease outbreaks with a focus on the case of the COVID-19 pandemic.

The findings of this study demonstrated the important contribution of the implemented public health measures in reducing the COVID-19 disease burden. Both vaccination and limiting mobility through lockdowns contributed to slowing the spread of infection, reducing severe illness and mortality and were cost-saving through reducing pressure on healthcare resource utilization. The activity also contributed to building capacity for economic evaluation within the Ministry of Health in preparation for future outbreaks.

projects.description:
WCO convened a partner’s forum in September to engage with civil society organizations (CSOs) in developing and implementing innovative evidence-based community engagement initiatives which address cross-cutting health issues pertaining to COVID-19. 

The forum analyzed enablers and barriers to getting COVID-19 vaccines, how to increase COVID-19 vaccine uptake among people at high risk of getting severely ill from COVID-19 in areas with low booster uptake, how to increase adherence to COVID-19 protective behaviors, prevention and control of NCDs amid the COVID-19 pandemic. A total of 33 participants from 22 CSOs/NGOs attended the forum. Following the meeting, 25 concept notes were received, reviewed and sifted to 5 proposals for further review. The selected proposal will be chosen for further activity implementation in 2023.

The Joint Team rendered substantial support to the Malaysian Government in ensuring sustainable funding, advancing prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV services and expanding HIV services to hard-to-reach communities. Technical support to the Malaysian Country Coordinating Mechanism and the Malaysian AIDS Council led to a successful Global Fund for HIV grant proposal for the 2022-2025 period. Focused on the establishment of resilient and sustainable systems for health (RSSH) and the expansion of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) as a method of HIV prevention, the application secured US$ 1.5 million for the procurement of PrEP for 18 primary care clinics across Malaysia until December 2024. More than US$ 1 million was also allocated to strengthen community-led programmes, the national health management information system, and monitoring and evaluation for RSSH (WHO).

Malaysia achieved all the process and outcome indicator targets set in the Elimination of Mother-to-child Transmission of HIV (EMTCT) and Syphilis plan for the 2017-2020 period. In 2022, the Joint Team provided extensive technical support for the development and submission of the EMTCT maintenance report and worked closely with the Regional and Global Validation Secretariat and the Ministry of Health to address concerns including human rights, gender equality and community engagement, which were raised by Global Validation Advisory Committee (GVAC) during its 2021 virtual mission (WHO).

The newly launched Reaching the Unreached (RTU) agenda helped to identify key cross-cutting issues affecting marginalized populations, including the high prevalence of communicable diseases such as tuberculosis in East Malaysia and in prisons and other closed settings through a collaboration with relevant stakeholders (WHO). Intense advocacy and technical support to the Ministry of Health also resulted in the Government recognizing the need to strengthen laboratory capacity by expanding point-of-care testing systems in high-burden areas to eliminate logistical barriers and improve access to healthcare services (WHO).

To expand access to HIV services among key and vulnerable populations, 138 refugees and asylum seekers living with HIV accessed antiretroviral treatment with support from the Joint Team. Nongovernmental organizations also received support in providing treatment adherence support services for 172 persons living with HIV enrolled on treatment, rehabilitative and nursing care for 12 extremely vulnerable refugees as well as sexual and reproductive health, gender-based violence and HIV information and counselling services for 935 hard-to-reach women and girls and their spouses through regular mobile outreach programmes in the Northern region of the Peninsular Malaysia. Additionally, 128 pregnant women and girls received antenatal care while 270 were given regular access to contraceptives through the mobile programmes (UNHCR).

Technical assistance was provided to the National Anti-drugs Agency of Malaysia on the transition towards voluntary-community based treatment and care of people who use drugs, as well as on “Strong Families” family-skills substance use prevention among children and adolescents. The Malaysian Prisons Department also benefitted from technical support on the delivery of comprehensive packages of HIV services for people in prisons (UNODC).

framework.name: People
framework.description: Leaving No One Behind- Ensuring a prosperous nation through inclusivity and well-being for all

children.name: By 2025, poor and vulnerable groups living in Malaysia benefit from more equity-focused and high-quality social services as well as a social protection system that ensures all have an adequate standard of living.
A more efficient, effective and sustainable social protection system is in place that provides increased protection against contingencies throughout the lifecycle.
Social services are strengthened to ensure universal access to high-quality, equity focused social services that promote social wellbeing for all.
Increased adoption of inclusive social norms and values and rejection of harmful practices, particularly against women and girls, and the creation of demand for services
By 2025, environmental sustainability and resilience are mainstreamed as priorities within the national development agenda, across all sectors and levels of society.
Transitioning national development towards a decarbonised pathway and a resource efficient economy through the adoption of green growth strategies and practices across all sectors.
Natural resources, biodiversity and ecosystems are sustainably managed, adequately protected and conserved for long-term economic and environmental sustainability.
Preparedness and resilience (especially of indigenous, poor, at-risk communities) against climate change, natural hazards, and disaster risks are strengthened.
By 2025, Malaysia is making meaningful progress towards an economy that is inclusive, innovative, and sustainable across all income groups and productive sectors.
Inclusive growth and decent work that also taps into new sources of economic growth and the Future of Work trends.
Further advances made towards women’s equality in the economy.

Adoption of corporate practices that are aligned to SDGs and international standards of upholding principles of social justice, transparency accountability and sustainability while promoting economic development.
Competitive, sustainable and inclusive urban development that supports social and economic well-being for the population.

framework.name: Peace
framework.description: Social Cohesion, Governance and Human Rights

children.name: By 2025, Malaysia has strengthened democratic governance, and all people living in Malaysia benefit from a more cohesive society, strengthened governance and participation.
children.description:
There has been an overall shift in Malaysia’s development planning focus from “macroeconomic resilience” to “more meaningful economic growth”34. A key tenet of this shift is embedded in governance reform through greater transparency and public-service efficiency35. A focus on good governance, accountability and transparency, at the institutional and individual level, and keeping social consciousness and environmental sustainability at the centre of economic growth have been identified as being critical to Malaysia escaping the “middle-income trap” and achieving its full potential, in line with the priorities of SDG 16, including peace/social cohesion, governance and human rights. The MTR of the Eleventh Plan lays out a holistic and high-impact agenda for governance reforms, reflecting the broad need for greater separation of powers across the executive, legislature and judiciary, strengthening checks and balances, and other specific aspects, including electoral reforms, strengthening anticorruption efforts, etc. The SPV 2030 also reinforces these reforms as continuing priorities.

One of the hallmarks of a democratic nation can be seen in the degree of independence, transparency and inclusivity of its institutions, as noted in the MTR of the Eleventh Plan’s agenda for governance reforms, and the inclusivity of its political processes — processes which, in essence, determine and reflect the ultimate will and representation of the people. These processes are seen in electoral institutions that are inclusive and responsive to the population, political parties that reflect the spectrum of values and ideologies of the society, and legislative bodies that are truly representative. The “Sustaining Peace and Good Governance Goal” (SDG 16) has specific significance for parliamentarians. SDG 16 aims to “promote peaceful and inclusive societies, providing access to justice for all and building effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels”, with targets 16.6 and 16.7 directly fitting with parliamentarian roles. Another important element is space for civil society, dissenting voices and freedom of media, which has regained ground in recent times, to be further consolidated and professionalised. In this regard, the Ministry of Home Affairs is in the process of amending the Printing Presses and Publications Act 1984. Malaysia’s legal framework should provide increased protection against discrimination, abuse, stigmatisation and harassment on the basis of age, gender, race, disability or other characteristics, and this protection should be effectively enforced.

The focus on greater accountability in the governance pillar of the MTR of the Eleventh Plan also means expanding public participation in policymaking, ensuring that development plans are inclusive, and taking into account local contexts and constituency-specific realities. Therefore, any significant reform of governance policies must necessarily touch on challenging issues, emphasising the need for inclusive engagement with stakeholders. The role of civil society in governance reform is vital in terms of it playing a constructive role in policy debates on reform, thereby ensuring inclusion as well as making civil society a partner in monitoring governance performance and in delivering public services to specific target communities.

The current state of federal-state-local government relations is also key. There is a need for increased policy coherence and implementation coordination across levels of government in order to enhance the effectiveness of development results in Malaysia. Thus, a clearer understanding of the linkages between processes and stronger and more extensive engagement at subnational levels are entry points for intervention.

Also important is the fact that, although Malaysia’s various plans and policies have articulated variations on the themes of social stability, social integration and social cohesion, the overall scope remains quite limited. In line with the MTR of the Eleventh Plan, a National Unity Advisory Council has been formed and emphasis has been placed on a needs-based approach and, with the SPV 2030, on equitable outcomes. In March 2020, a new Ministry of National Unity was formed to take this important agenda forward. Consistent engagement at all levels (policy, institutional and community) is required to holistically address these issues and ensure inclusion.

The COVID-19 crisis has disproportionately impacted poor and vulnerable groups. Malaysia recorded a spike in gender-based violence (GBV), and the lack of routine data collection and inclusion of GBV in national surveys hampers efforts to mitigate its prevalence in an effective manner. The pandemic has further deepened the issues faced by undocumented persons, migrants, refugees and asylum seekers – in relation to legal access to services and squalid living conditions that have put them at greater risk of infection.

Finally, it is essential to note that the inclusion and participation of women, youth and children remains a major challenge. This is evidenced by the low political participation of women (as measured by their active engagement and parity in leadership positions or in the legislature). For instance, while women make up almost 60 per cent of the civil service (excluding the police and the military), the 14th General Elections of 2018 and the current Government brought about only five women ministers and four deputy ministers (12.9 per cent); 14.4 per cent of seats in the lower house of Parliament, and only 19.4 per cent of seats in the upper house36. In the corporate sector, women only hold 15.7 per cent of board seats in publicly-listed companies (against a target of 30 per cent)37. Youth under 3038 also constitute a significant proportion of Malaysia’s population, and, with the recent lowering of the voting age to 18, youth will form a significant proportion of the electorate in the future. Currently, there are inadequate opportunities for the engagement and participation of adolescents in national and subnational decision-making processes that affect their well-being, as well as in political processes. Responding to these challenges will be key to: ensuring that the potential of Malaysia’s youthful human capital is maximised; building a cohesive, inclusive and caring society; and developing values and gender and social norms to allow young people to feel that they have a stake in the nation’s development, and that they have the power and opportunity to contribute to decision-making that affects them. Hence, additional targeted interventions aimed at youth participation are needed, especially in decision making, productive work, social cohesion and political processes.

children.name: Malaysia makes significant progress towards inter-ethnic and cultural harmony and cohesion.
Institutions are more capable of undertaking inclusive political processes and are more citizen-centric and protective of fundamental freedoms.

The system of checks and balances across branches of government is strengthened at national and subnational levels, core government functions are more responsive and efficient, and people have better access to services
Enhancing Results through Coordination and Partnerships
children.description: The results that the UN in Malaysia is aspiring to contribute to over the next five years, as set out in the Strategic Priority Areas and Collaborative Outputs in this UNSDCF, will be enhanced through effective coordination and building of critical partnerships, primarily with the Government at national and subnational levels, and with the private sector, civil society and academia – led by the UN Resident Coordinator System and SDG Results Group chaired by the UN Resident Coordinator. The Office of the UN Resident Coordinator will facilitate the provision of UN technical assistance upon request by state governments.
